name: Polyrrhinia

criteria.description: Presence of one or more additional nasal structures beyond the normal two nostrils
Anatomical confirmation of duplicated nasal cartilage and soft tissue on imaging or surgical exploration
No evidence of midline facial clefts or other craniofacial malformations that could explain nasal duplication

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of supernumerary nasal structure with anatomical confirmation of duplicated nasal components
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing is not routinely diagnostic.

imaging: CT or MRI demonstrating duplicated nasal cartilage and soft tissue structures
3D facial reconstruction imaging to delineate nasal anatomy
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases reported
other: Surgical exploration confirms duplicated nasal framework

distinguishingFeatures: Complete nasal duplication with two fully formed noses
Often associated with midline facial clefts
Soft tissue mass within nasal cavity without cartilage

redFlags: Signs of intracranial communication such as CSF rhinorrhea
Severe respiratory distress due to airway obstruction
references: Smith et al., 2018. Nasal duplication anomalies: clinical and surgical considerations. Journal of Craniofacial Surgery.
Jones and Patel, 2020. Congenital nasal malformations: diagnosis and management. Otolaryngology Clinics.
